jobs.description: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE: We are looking for a Senior Data Center Technician Lead to join our VSEI Field Services team supporting client data center environments in the Phoenix, Arizona area. This is a hands-on technical lead opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex server issues while also helping guide and support other technicians. In this highly visible role, you will work alongside a team of data center technicians while serving as a key connection between the technical team, project managers, and leadership. You will lead daily huddles, help resolve technical blockers, maintain visibility into ticket and project status, and provide clear updates to leadership. You will also remain hands-on, working directly with servers and managing your own tickets. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced data center technician looking to expand beyond an individual contributor role, increase leadership exposure, and continue developing toward future technical leadership or management opportunities. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a strong communicator who is comfortable working with both hands-on technicians and leadership. You are organized, technically curious, collaborative, and able to maintain a big-picture view of site operations while also diving into technical issues when needed. You thrive in a fast-paced data center environment, enjoy helping others work through technical challenges, and can quickly learn new systems and processes. You are comfortable taking ownership, communicating blockers and progress, and balancing your own workload while serving as a technical resource for the broader team. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Lead daily team huddles to communicate priorities, ticket activity, operational changes, technical blockers, and other important site updates. Provide technical guidance and hands-on assistance to data center technicians troubleshooting server-related issues. Perform hands-on server troubleshooting, break/fix activities, and assigned ticket work within the data center environment. Maintain visibility into the site's active ticket queue, including status, blockers, and work progression. Serve as a liaison between technicians, project managers, and management to ensure information and operational updates are communicated effectively. Coordinate parts checkout and provide hands-on support to technicians working on server hardware. Provide daily roll call, huddle notes, and end-of-day ticket status updates. During the first 30 days, become familiar with team processes, systems, and the technical environment. Within the first 60 to 90 days, develop proficiency with administrative responsibilities, supported SKUs, and day-to-day technical support for the technician team. Long term, serve as a trusted higher-level technical resource who can assist technicians with troubleshooting and drive effective communication around site activities and ticket issues. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience working in data center environments and supporting server hardware. Strong server break/fix, troubleshooting, and problem-analysis skills. Experience with server hardware installation, configuration, and server-side management. Working knowledge of PowerShell and Linux command-line environments. Knowledge of networking equipment and its use when troubleshooting technical issues. Experience managing technical tickets, identifying blockers, and communicating status and progress. Experience providing technical guidance or support to other technicians is preferred. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: High school diploma or GED desired. College-level education in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline is preferred. CompTIA A+ or an equivalent technology certification is preferred. LOCATION: Phoenix, Arizona This role supports client data center locations and follows a Sunday through Wednesday, 6:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. schedule, working four 10-hour days per week. The position involves 25% to 50% travel, primarily between data centers within the local area. Travel outside the local area may occasionally be requested but is not mandatory. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Who are we?

Tripledot Studios is one of the largest independent mobile games companies in the world.

We are a multi-award-winning organisation, with a global 2,500+ strong team across 12 studios.

Our expanded portfolio includes some of the biggest titles in mobile gaming, collectively reaching top chart positions around the world and engaging over 25 million daily active users.

Tripledot’s guiding principle is that when people love what they do, what they do will be loved by others.

We’re building a company we’re proud of. One filled with driven, incredibly smart and detail-orientated people, who LOVE making games.

Our ambition is to be the most successful games company in the world, and we’re just getting started.

The role is working within our studio: PuzzlePlay

Puzzleplay is Tripledot’s new player rewards platform, designed to make playing our games even more fun and engaging. By playing our casual, free to play mobile games, users can earn points, complete challenges, and win real prizes. It’s our way of giving back to players and rewarding them for doing what they already love. Puzzleplay is a key part of our growth strategy, combining smart engagement mechanics with high-quality game content.

Role Overview

Puzzleplay at Tripledot Studios is looking for a data analyst to own the fraud side of its user segmentation work. The team is building a system that combines fraud and activity signals to understand users and inform revenue-share decisions. You'll work with the analyst responsible for gameplay signals, alongside product and data colleagues, to keep that system useful as fraud patterns change.

Fraud patterns keep changing, so you'll regularly revisit the signals behind the segments and help the product team decide which verification methods make sense in each market.

This role is open to candidates based in Europe; Warsaw is preferred, where several of the people you'll work with are based.

Key Responsibilities

• Review fraud signals regularly, adding, removing and refining them to distinguish suspicious activity from legitimate users. Signals under consideration include IP spoofing, VPN use and unusual play patterns.
• Own the fraud-related segments of the user segmentation system, from deciding how signals should be interpreted to monitoring how well the categories work over time.
• Work with the product team on fraud verification tools for different markets. The team currently uses FaceTec for facial verification and may need other methods, such as ID scanning or phone verification, in other countries.
• Investigate users flagged for manual review, including ambiguous cases in the Tremendous queue, and look for ways to improve the review process.
• Identify gaps in the available signals and recommend third-party tools for the product roadmap where they would help.

Required Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

• Hands-on experience using data to investigate fraud and shape detection or prevention decisions, not just working alongside a fraud team.
• Experience designing or improving fraud signals, user segments or review processes, with an interest in how those decisions change as tactics evolve.
• The ability to work with product and other teams to turn analysis into operational fraud controls.

Grow Your Skills, Grow Your Potential

The Role General Motors is seeking a Manager, Product Research - Product Experience Clinics & KPIs to lead a team of researchers and/or analysts within Global Customer Research (GCR) Product Research. This leader will bring the voice of the customer into GM’s vehicle software, digital experiences, features, and emerging technologies. The Manager partners with Program Management and Software Product teams to understand and anticipate customer needs, vehicle-usage contexts, and experience opportunities in, on, and around the vehicle. The role supports the development of planned customer experiences—software-orchestrated coordination of vehicle features—that meet customer needs and exceed expectations, enabling meaningful innovation and industry-leading CX/UX. This role is ideal for a customer-centered research leader who combines strong project execution and people leadership with the ability to turn complex customer learning into clear product direction. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted research partner to stakeholders, guide a portfolio of bespoke research, and develop a capable team that delivers rigorous, timely, and actionable insight.
